argument: For related reactions sharing a mechanism, activation energy often follows $E_a\approx E_0+\alpha\Delta H$. This linear free-energy relation explains why thermodynamic binding trends can predict kinetic barriers and underlies catalyst volcano plots.
boundary: The relation is local to a reaction family and mechanism.
Changes in transition-state structure, coverage, solvent, or surface can break linearity.
Approximate barrier prediction does not replace explicit kinetics when selectivity is critical.
claim: For related reactions sharing a mechanism, activation energy often follows $E_a\approx E_0+\alpha\Delta H$. This linear free-energy relation explains why thermodynamic binding trends can predict kinetic barriers and underlies catalyst volcano plots.
interpretation: Principia should attach the reaction family and mechanism; cross-family extrapolation is a major failure mode.
